questions.question: What was the theme of Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan?

options.text: Designing Future Society for Our Lives
Feeding the Planet, Energy for Life

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Designing Future Society for Our Lives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The theme for Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan, is **"Designing Future Society for Our Lives"**, emphasizing innovative solutions for global challenges.
 
• Expo 2025 will aim to explore sustainable development goals (SDGs) and address pressing global issues such as health, environment, and technology.
 
• It will be held on **Yumeshima Island, Osaka**, from **April 13 to October 13, 2025**.
 
• The event is expected to attract over **28 million visitors** from around the world, fostering cultural and technological exchange.
 
• The Expo is being organized by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE), the intergovernmental organization responsible for overseeing world exhibitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Expos:**

 
 
• World Expos, also known as World Fairs, are large international exhibitions showcasing achievements in science, technology, art, and culture.
 
• The first World Expo was held in **London in 1851**, called "The Great Exhibition."
 
• They are organized by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE) and occur every five years.
 
 
 
• **Osaka's Role in Expo History:**
 
 
• Osaka previously hosted the **Expo 1970**, which was the first World Expo held in Japan.
 
• The theme of Expo 1970 was **"Progress and Harmony for Mankind."**
 
• It attracted 64 million visitors, making it one of the most successful Expos in history.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Expo 2025 aligns with the United Nations' **17 Sustainable Development Goals**, promoting global collaboration for a better future.
 
• Key focus areas include climate action, health and well-being, and technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Yumeshima Island:**
 
 
• Yumeshima is a man-made island in Osaka Bay, chosen as the venue for Expo 2025.
 
• It is being developed as a hub for innovation, sustainability, and tourism.
 
• The island will also host integrated resort facilities, including casinos, after the Expo.

questions.question: As of April 2025, Similipal - designated as the second national park of the state - is located in:
questions.solution:

• The park is part of the **Similipal-Kuldiha-Hadgarh Elephant Reserve**, which comes under the **Mayurbhanj district** of Odisha.
 
• It was declared a **national park in 1980** and is recognized as the **second national park** of the state.
 
• The name "Similipal" is derived from the abundance of **Semul trees (silk cotton trees)**, which bloom vividly in this region.
 
• Similipal is known for its **rich biodiversity**, including species like **Bengal tigers, Asian elephants, leopards, and gaurs**.
 
• The park also features a wide range of **flora and fauna**, with a mix of tropical evergreen forests, deciduous forests, and grasslands.
 
• It is famous for its **picturesque waterfalls** like **Barehipani** and **Joranda**, which are major attractions for visitors.
 
• Similipal was designated as a **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in the year **2009**.
 
• The area is significant for its indigenous tribal population, including the **Ho, Munda, and Santhal tribes**, who reside in and around the park.
 
• Similipal plays a critical role in **conservation efforts** for endangered species and protecting the natural ecosystem of the Eastern Ghats region.

• **Madhya Pradesh**__

• The state boasts famous national parks like **Kanha National Park**, **Bandhavgarh National Park**, and **Pench National Park**.
 
• Similipal, however, is not located in Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Assam**__

• The state also has other wildlife sanctuaries like **Manas National Park** and **Dibru-Saikhowa National Park**.

• **Maharashtra** has a significant political landscape where BJP has traditionally secured a large number of seats due to its strong electoral base and alliance with other political groups.
 
• **Delhi**, although a smaller state in terms of Assembly seats, saw a notable number of BJP wins, attributed to its focus on urban development and nationalistic campaigns.
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir** witnessed BJP's growing influence, especially in the Jammu region, following the abrogation of **Article 370**, leading to increased support in this Union Territory.
 
• **Jharkhand**, a state with a strong tribal demographic, has traditionally been a challenging region for the BJP compared to the other states listed, resulting in fewer seats.
 
• The order reflects the political strategy, regional popularity, and voter base of the BJP in the respective states during the mentioned elections.

• Jammu and Kashmir, now a Union Territory, has a total of 90 assembly seats, with BJP performing well in its stronghold regions.

questions.question: Where did the fifth session of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC-5) to end plastic pollution take place?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **fifth session of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC-5)** to end plastic pollution was held in **Busan, South Korea.**
 
• This session is part of the global effort under the United Nations to develop an **international legally binding instrument** to address the issue of plastic pollution.
 
• The INC sessions are aimed at tackling the growing challenge of **plastic waste** and its impact on **marine ecosystems, human health, and biodiversity.**
 
• Busan is a significant location for hosting such international events due to its role as a **global hub for trade and environmental initiatives.**
 
• The sessions focus on the **life cycle of plastics**, covering production, design, waste management, and recycling.
 
• South Korea has been actively involved in **international environmental policies** and has taken measures to address **plastic waste management** within its borders.
 
• The INC-5 session is a continuation of the global series initiated by the **United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA).**
 
• The meeting also emphasized the need for **collaborative efforts** among nations to curb plastic pollution through **policy frameworks, innovation, and public awareness campaigns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tokyo, Japan**__

 __
 
• **Tokyo** is the capital city of Japan and a major global hub for **technology, innovation, and international diplomacy.**
 
• While Japan is actively involved in addressing **plastic pollution**, Tokyo was not the location for the INC-5 session.
 
• Japan has implemented various measures such as **plastic bag charges** to reduce plastic waste.
 
 
 
• **Nairobi, Kenya**__
 __
 
• **Nairobi** is the headquarters of the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).**
 
• The **first session** of the INC to combat plastic pollution was held in Nairobi, highlighting its importance as a center for **environmental negotiations.**
 
• Kenya has been a pioneer in **plastic bag bans**, showcasing its commitment to combating pollution.
 
 
 
• **Berlin, Germany**__
 
 
• **Berlin** is a leading city in Europe for hosting **climate and environmental policy discussions.**
 
• Germany has one of the most advanced **waste management systems** in the world and plays a key role in global efforts to reduce plastic pollution.
 
• Although Berlin was not chosen for INC-5, Germany has been actively participating in the INC sessions.

questions.question: In December 2024, which day honoured Dr BR Ambedkar’s contribution to social justice?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Mahaparinirvan Diwas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahaparinirvan Diwas** is observed on **6th December** every year to honor the contributions of **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the architect of the Indian Constitution, towards social justice, equality, and empowerment.
 
• The term **Mahaparinirvan** signifies the attainment of ultimate liberation or salvation, which is a Buddhist concept.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar, a staunch advocate of **Dalit rights**, passed away on **6th December 1956**, and the day has been observed as Mahaparinirvan Diwas since then.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar was instrumental in combating **social discrimination**, particularly towards the marginalized sections of society.
 
• On this day, people across India pay homage to Dr. Ambedkar by visiting his memorial at **Chaitya Bhoomi** in Mumbai.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar's work in the fields of **law, economics, and social reform** continues to inspire millions of people worldwide.
 
• He was awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian honor, posthumously in **1990**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitution Awareness Day**__

 __
 
• **Constitution Awareness Day** is celebrated on **26th November**, the day the Indian Constitution was adopted in **1949**.
 
• The day is also referred to as **Constitution Day** or **Samvidhan Divas**.
 
• It is observed to spread awareness about the importance of the Indian Constitution and its role in ensuring **democracy and justice**.
 
 
 
• **National Equality Day**__
 __
 
• While the term **National Equality Day** is significant, it is not officially recognized or associated with Dr. Ambedkar's contributions.
 
• The concept focuses on promoting **equal rights** and opportunities for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Ambedkar Smriti Diwas**__
 
 
• While it may sound relevant, **Ambedkar Smriti Diwas** is not an officially recognized term for the day honoring Dr. Ambedkar.
 
• The official day for commemorating Dr. Ambedkar’s contributions is **Mahaparinirvan Diwas**.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above in rural India during the period 2022-23, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) annual report 2022-23?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **unemployment rate** for persons aged **15 years and above** in **rural India** during the period **2022-23** was **2.4% (0.024).**
 
• This data was reported in the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Annual Report 2022-23**, which is conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The **unemployment rate** is calculated as the percentage of unemployed persons in the labor force (both employed and unemployed) during the reference period.
 
• The **rural unemployment rate** is generally lower than the urban unemployment rate due to the availability of **agriculture-based employment** in rural areas.
 
• The PLFS aims to provide reliable estimates of the **labour force indicators**, such as employment, unemployment, and labor participation rates, across **rural and urban regions** of India.
 
• This report helps the government and policymakers to frame **employment and labor policies** to address the challenges of unemployment in India.

__
 
• **Importance of the PLFS:**__

 __
 
• The PLFS is a significant survey for understanding the **employment dynamics** in India.
 
• It provides data on **labor force participation rate (LFPR)**, **worker population ratio (WPR)**, and **unemployment rate (UR)**.
 
• The survey is conducted on a **quarterly basis for urban areas** and an **annual basis for rural and urban combined estimates.**
 
 
 
• **Rural Employment in India:**__
 __
 
• Agriculture remains the **primary source of employment** in rural India, employing a large percentage of the rural workforce.
 
• Other significant employment sectors in rural areas include **construction, manufacturing, and services.**
 
• Government programs like **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** play a crucial role in providing employment in rural regions.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Trends:**__
 
 
• The unemployment rate in rural areas is lower due to the prevalence of **informal and seasonal employment.**
 
• However, issues like **underemployment** and **disguised unemployment** are common in rural areas.

questions.question: Which country's federal election was held on 3 May 2025 to elect members of its 48th Parliament?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Australia** holds federal elections to elect members of its **Parliament**, which consists of the **House of Representatives** and the **Senate**.
 
• The election date is determined by the **Governor-General** on the advice of the Prime Minister. In this case, the election was held on **3 May 2025**.
 
• The federal election is conducted by the **Australian Electoral Commission (AEC)**, which ensures the process adheres to democratic standards.
 
• Australia operates under a **compulsory voting system**, meaning all eligible citizens are required to vote in federal elections.
 
• The electoral system used for the House of Representatives is the **preferential voting system**, while the Senate uses a **proportional representation system**.
 
• The elected members of the House of Representatives serve for a term of **three years**, and the Senate members serve for a term of **six years**, with half of the Senate seats up for election every three years.
 
• Australia's federal elections play a crucial role in shaping the country’s governance, as they determine the composition of the government and opposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Canada**__

 __
 
• **Canada** holds federal elections typically every **four years**, but the actual timing depends on the dissolution of Parliament.
 
• Canada operates under a **parliamentary system** with a bicameral legislature consisting of the **House of Commons** and the **Senate**.
 
• The elections are governed by the **Canada Elections Act** and conducted by **Elections Canada**.
 
 
 
• **New Zealand**__
 __
 
• **New Zealand** has a unicameral parliamentary system, with elections held every **three years**.
 
• Elections in New Zealand use the **Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) system**, combining both electorate and party votes.
 
• The elections are managed by the **Electoral Commission**.
 
 
 
• **United Kingdom**__
 
 
• The **United Kingdom** holds general elections typically every **five years** to elect members of the **House of Commons**.
 
• The UK operates under a **first-past-the-post electoral system**, where the candidate with the most votes in each constituency wins.
 
• Elections in the UK are managed by the **Electoral Commission** and overseen by local returning officers.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded with the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award for research in Diabetes in July 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Jitendra Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Jitendra Singh, a renowned diabetologist and an active researcher in diabetes, was awarded the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award for research in Diabetes in July 2024.
 
• The award recognizes his significant contributions to the field of diabetes management, treatment, and prevention strategies over the years.
 
• Dr. Jitendra Singh has authored numerous research papers and publications on the subject, providing valuable insights into diabetes care.
 
• He has also played a pivotal role in promoting awareness about diabetes and its complications in India.
 
• This recognition highlights his lifelong dedication to improving the lives of individuals affected by diabetes through both clinical practice and research.

• **Diabetes Overview:**

 
 
• Diabetes is a chronic condition characterized by high blood sugar levels due to the body's inability to produce or effectively use insulin.
 
• There are three main types of diabetes: Type 1, Type 2, and gestational diabetes.
 
• Type 2 diabetes is the most common form, often linked to lifestyle factors such as diet and physical activity.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Diabetes in India:**
 
 
• India is considered the diabetes capital of the world, with over 77 million people diagnosed with diabetes as of 2023.
 
• The rising prevalence of diabetes has been attributed to urbanization, sedentary lifestyles, and unhealthy dietary habits.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Research in Diabetes:**

• Advancements in diabetes research have led to innovations such as insulin analogs, continuous glucose monitoring systems, and artificial pancreas technology.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• Programs like the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases, and Stroke (NPCDCS) aim to combat diabetes and related disorders.
 
• Awareness campaigns and free screening initiatives are regularly conducted to educate the public and promote early diagnosis.

questions.question: The Tonnage Tax Scheme, seen in Union Budget 2025-26, is associated with taxing which sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shipping activities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tonnage Tax Scheme is a specialized taxation policy aimed at **shipping companies**, providing a simplified and concessional tax regime.
 
• Under this scheme, shipping companies are taxed based on the tonnage capacity of their ships rather than their profits, ensuring **stability in tax liabilities**.
 
• The objective is to promote the **growth of the shipping sector** by reducing the compliance burden and incentivizing investments in maritime activities.
 
• Introduced in India in 2004, the scheme aligns with global practices adopted in countries like the UK and Singapore to enhance competitiveness in international shipping.
 
• In the Union Budget 2025-26, further emphasis was placed on **expanding and strengthening shipping activities** under the Tonnage Tax Scheme to bolster India's maritime trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tonnage Tax:**

 
 
• A taxation mechanism where shipping companies are taxed on the basis of the net tonnage of their vessels rather than their actual income or profits.
 
• It offers predictability and reduces administrative complexities in tax calculations for shipping operators.
 
 
 
• **Significance for India:**
 
 
• India's shipping industry plays a crucial role in global trade, handling approximately 95% of the country's trade by volume.
 
• The Tonnage Tax Scheme helps Indian shipping companies compete globally by ensuring a level playing field.
 
 
 
• **Global Practices:**
 
 
• Countries like the UK, Singapore, and Japan have implemented similar tonnage tax regimes to attract shipping businesses and enhance their maritime economies.
 
• These policies align with international norms, encouraging investment and fleet expansion.
 
 
 
• **Maritime Development in India:**
 
 
• India has launched several initiatives, such as the Sagarmala Project, to modernize ports and improve the efficiency of maritime logistics.
 
• The Tonnage Tax Scheme complements these efforts by supporting long-term growth in shipping and maritime trade.

questions.question: In March 2025, which day was celebrated to promote the use of generic medicines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jan Aushadhi Diwas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jan Aushadhi Diwas** is celebrated annually on **March 7th** to create awareness and promote the use of generic medicines.
 
• The initiative is part of the **Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)**, a government scheme launched to provide affordable and quality medicines to all citizens.
 
• Generic medicines, which are distributed through Jan Aushadhi Kendras, are **50% to 90% cheaper** than branded medicines, ensuring affordability for the general public.
 
• Jan Aushadhi Kendras serve as a crucial step towards **accessible healthcare** by offering medicines at reduced costs, benefiting especially the economically weaker sections.
 
• In March 2025, Jan Aushadhi Diwas was celebrated to emphasize the role of generic medicines in reducing healthcare costs and improving accessibility across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Generic Medicines:**

 
 
• Generic medicines are drugs that are chemically identical to branded drugs but are sold under their chemical name rather than a brand name.
 
• They are approved by the regulatory authorities for their efficacy, safety, and quality.
 
• Generic medicines help reduce the financial burden of healthcare on the population.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP):**
 
 
• Launched in 2008 and revamped under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi, PMBJP aims to provide affordable medicines through a network of Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
 
• These Kendras are functional across the country, with over 9,000 outlets as of 2023.
 
• The program ensures the availability of quality medicines certified by the Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India (BPPI).
 
 
 
• **Health Impact:**
 
 
• Jan Aushadhi Kendras play a critical role in improving healthcare access for low-income and rural communities.
 
• They contribute towards reducing the financial stress related to medical expenses, enabling better health outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Awareness Campaigns:**
 
 
• Events like Jan Aushadhi Diwas are used to spread information about generic medicines and their benefits.
 
• These campaigns aim to break misconceptions about the efficacy of generic drugs and encourage public trust.
